answer: Dishonest graders are slashed and their stake is redistributed, which means a Sybil cluster that tries to vote as a bloc will, on average, lose more from slashing than it gains from manipulating a single verdict. The upshot is a network where trust is a resource you earn, not a quantity you can mint — and that is what keeps Sybil attacks economically unviable.. It is effective because voting power is weighted by verifiable work over time, so a fresh flood of accounts cannot manufacture a decisive vote. Consider a copper as the anchor of the cost.
